chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man raised his head from prostration and doubted before he sat upright, so he did not know if he had prostrated or not. He said: 'He prostrates.' I said: And a man rose from his prostration and doubted before he stood upright, so he did not know if he had prostrated or not. He said: 'He prostrates.'

key_terms.أَسْجَدَ أَمْ لَمْ يَسْجُدْ: Did he prostrate or not he prostrated

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one doubts whether they prostrated before sitting up or standing up in prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific ruling for *shakk* (doubt) occurring during the transition phases of prayer, distinguishing it from doubts after full completion. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that if one doubts whether a prostration was completed before fully sitting or standing, the default assumption is that it was not performed, necessitating an additional *sujood al-shakk* to ensure the prayer's validity. This ruling reflects the Shia principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) applied to ritual acts, ensuring worshippers do not leave obligatory components undone due to uncertainty.
